## How to retrieve sub‑domain descriptors for `example.org`

### 1. Endpoint

```
GET https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/relationships
```

### 2. Query parameters

| Parameter            | Value                     | Description                                 |
|----------------------|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `relationship_type` | `subdomains`              | Only return objects that are sub‑domains   |
| `limit`              | `10`                      | Return at most 10 results                  |
| `continuation_cursor`| `abc`                     | Resume from this cursor (if you’re paging) |

### 3. Headers

```http
x-apikey: my_api
Accept: application/json
```

### 4. Example `curl` command

```bash
curl -X GET \
  "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/relationships?relationship_type=subdomains&limit=10&continuation_cursor=abc" \
  -H "x-apikey: my_api" \
  -H "Accept: application/json"
```

### 5. Expected response (simplified)

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "sub1.example.org",
      "type": "domains",
      "attributes": {
        "last_analysis_stats": { ... },
        "last_analysis_date": 1700000000,
        ...
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "sub2.example.org",
      "type": "domains",
      "attributes": { ... }
    },
    ...
  ],
  "meta": {
    "continuation_cursor": "def",
    "total": 42
  }
}
```

> **Note**: The API returns the full object by default. If you only want the IDs and a few context attributes, you can trim the response on your side or use the `fields` query parameter (e.g., `fields=id,attributes.last_analysis_stats`) to limit what’s returned.

---

## Quick Python snippet

```python
import requests

url = "https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/example.org/relationships"
params = {
    "relationship_type": "subdomains",
    "limit": 10,
    "continuation_cursor": "abc",
    "fields": "id,attributes.last_analysis_stats"
}
headers = {
    "x-apikey": "my_api",
    "Accept": "application/json"
}

resp = requests.get(url, headers=headers, params=params)
print(resp.json())
```

This will give you a JSON object containing only the IDs and the requested context attributes for each sub‑domain.
